faq.answer: No. Leadership may follow election, seniority, expertise, employment, or collective need. The subtype hypothesis requires recurring connection attention organized through group usefulness and evidence from role changes.
faq.question: Does community leadership establish social Type Two?

faq.answer: Introductions and information show how usefulness operates in practice. Recording who benefits, who is excluded, and whether access depends on gratitude or status makes the hypothesis testable without moral ranking.
faq.question: Why observe who receives network access?

faq.answer: Contribution that ends with role loss, selective access aimed at recognition, or stronger repeated attention to private comfort or one relationship would weaken it. Institutional incentives should be examined first.
faq.question: What weakens the group usefulness hypothesis?

sections.body_md: The hypothesis combines Type Two connection attention with a social label for networks, contribution, and a useful place in the group. Organizing people may instead reflect leadership duty, community norms, political skill, fundraising, or institutional incentives.
sections.title: Describe group usefulness provisionally

sections.body_md: This matched comparison asks about group role and practical comfort by observing whether attention first moves toward a useful place in the group, receiving care, or concentrated connection with one person. Hold the request and available resources as constant as possible.
sections.title: Compare group, practical, and focused connection

sections.body_md: Social is traditional organizing vocabulary rather than evidence about bodily mechanisms. It makes no claims about neural organization or unchanging social function, and it establishes no leadership value, popularity, fairness, or automatic group orientation.
sections.title: Keep social language non-mechanistic

sections.body_md: Subtype traditions vary in how they describe influence, ambition, visibility, and countertypical service. Test the specific group-usefulness claim and let low-status, private, or contradictory events revise it.
sections.title: Expect schools to describe status differently

sections.body_md: Committee roles, community organizing, sales, fundraising, politics, and seniority can reward introductions and broad contribution. Compare behavior after role loss, lower visibility, and reduced access before retaining the subtype.
sections.title: Test leadership and network incentives

sections.body_md: A social Type Two counterexample weakens a group usefulness hypothesis when contribution stops after status loss, access is shared only for recognition, or matched situations repeatedly prioritize private comfort or one bond.
sections.title: Use role transfer as disconfirming evidence

sections.body_md: Instrument-specific subtype evidence does not justify broad claims about culture, leadership, or personal value. Observe access, consent, reciprocity, and role incentives without turning contribution into identity.
sections.title: Keep group conclusions modest

sections.body_md:
Duration: 5

Context: Choose one introduction, one group task, and one event where a useful role passes to another person while needs remain visible.

Observable signal: Record who receives access, what contribution is made, which status or recognition is available, and what continues after the role changes.

Page-specific signal: Compare group usefulness with practical comfort and focused one-person connection under a similar request.

Alternative explanation: Test elected duty, seniority, employment, fundraising, political skill, institutional incentives, and community norms against the subtype.

Reflection prompt: Identify the event where contribution followed status most closely and state whether role incentives now explain more than the subtype.

seo.description: Social Type Two is a traditional type-by-instinct hypothesis in which Two attention to needs and connection may appear through group roles, networks, contribution, and being useful to a wider circle. Two group usefulness is observable, but position, leadership duty, or community incentives may explain it.
seo.title: Social Type Two: group usefulness as a provisional subtype hypothesis
